Quick triage notes (what I see so far):
- Dedicated pool for Clearsumm in us-west-2 saw a sharp queue-depth increase starting 07:38 PT; avg seq_len for affected requests spiked to ~450 tokens (vs baseline ~60).
- Autoscaler triggered new hosts but we saw a ~2.5min median scale delay for GPUs to become schedulable (node init + warmup + model load). During that window requests backed up -> gateway 502/503 and 429s from per-route rate limiter.
- We also observed several long-running synchronous requests that pinned KV caches and prevented efficient batching. This increased per-token latency and blocked the concurrent request slots on several dedicated GPU instances.

Immediate mitigations I pushed (09:00):
- Enabled aggressive fallback routing for routes associated with Clearsumm: up to 20% of traffic routed to the hosted pool (lower-cost/fast-boot instances) to shed load from the Dedicated pool.
- Shortened model-variant boot profile (force quantized variant) for new instances to reduce load time.
- Temporarily increased concurrency cap for their dedicated pool by +15% where safe.

I'll continue with heap/log grabs and coordinate with Vivek on whether we need to spin reserve capacity for the next 24h.

Ben Carter
Head of Platform Ops
Redwood Inference

From: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
To: ben_carter@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2027 10:24:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: RE: Fwd: spike of 5xx/429 this morning - production degraded

Status update / technical summary:
- Root cause (prelim): a multi-tenant workload pattern with a sudden influx of long-context requests saturated KV cache slots and filled the GPU scheduling window. Autoscaler reacted but model cold-start + shard loading time (especially for fp16/full variants) caused a tail in capacity availability. During the lag, per-route token-based throttles returned 429s and upstream load balancers returned 502/503.
- Observed metrics: GPU utilization reached sustained 98% on 7 hosts, queue depth 600+ for the dedicated pool, mean time-to-sched 150s for cold nodes before our boot-profile adjustments.
- Immediate actions taken:
  * Forced fallback routing (20%) to hosted pool to restore throughput and reduce queue pressure.
  * Applied temporary prefix caching for common prompt templates used by Clearsumm to reduce compute per request.
  * Deployed a hot-reserve of 2 pre-warmed nodes for Clearsumm's pool (30-min hold) to cover the ramp.

Next steps (ETA):
- Short-term (0-2h): monitor the fallback route and host metrics; if stable, start gradual traffic re-routing back. Expected visible improvement 15-30 minutes after warm nodes are active.
- Mid-term (today): refine autoscaler thresholds and reduce cold-start model size for their most-used route.
- Post-incident: propose model-variant pinning and burst capacity SLA (reserved nodes) for Clearsumm; ops can discuss pricing.

I'll join the customer bridge if needed.

Vivek Kulkarni
SRE Lead — Dedicated Pools
Redwood Inference

Jared / Team —

Thank you for the sample logs and for flagging this quickly. Quick summary of what happened and what we did:
- Cause: a sudden burst of long-context requests exhausted KV slots in your Dedicated pool and autoscaler lag meant capacity didn't appear fast enough; that combination produced a wave of 5xx/429 errors.
- Immediate mitigations we applied: routed ~20% of traffic to our hosted pool while we pre-warmed 2 reserve nodes in your dedicated pool; forced quantized model variants to reduce cold-start time; applied short-lived prefix caching for common prompts. Those changes reduced queue depth and error rate within ~25 minutes; latency and success rate are currently trending back to baseline.

Next steps and asks:
1) Postmortem: our engineering team will produce a short postmortem with timelines and concrete prevention actions (today EOD).
2) Preventive options for you: reserve burst capacity (pre-warmed nodes) for high-throughput windows, route-level rate limits and graceful-degradation policies, or a small model-variant pin for critical routes. Ben / Vivek will share recommended config and a cost estimate.
3) Please share any replay traces or sample prompts that correlate with this window so we can further optimize batching/prefix caching.

We're sorry for the disruption — I will keep you updated hourly until we confirm stability.

Best,
